facts.text: Dolly Parton's nephew, Bryan Seaver, has been terminated from his position managing security at the late country music icon's properties.
Seaver, who had served as the head of security and notably announced Parton's passing last month, received a dismissal notice on September 16.
Reports further indicated that new security personnel have already been assigned to oversee Parton's homes in Nashville, along with her museum and warehouse.
Dolly Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver has reportedly been fired from his longtime role as the head of security for the late country star's properties.

Seaver, the family representative who announced Parton's death last month at the age of 80 , received a termination notice September 16 saying that he and his security guard employees had been dismissed, according to TMZ .
Seaver, who is the son of Parton's younger sister Cassie, announced the news on behalf of the country legend's family in a video shared on her social media accounts.
Dolly Parton's nephew, Bryan Seaver, was reportedly fired as head of security amid an ongoing dispute over the singer's estate.

They added "We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much."Meanwhile, the news of Seaver's firing has caused ripples online as many have seen this as an escalation of the estate dispute.
The publication reportedly has the termination notice sent to Seaver which informed him that he and his company were immediately dismissed from all of Parton's properties.
They told TMZ that Seaver and his team were ‘dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions’ taken since Parton passed away.
Dolly Parton’s nephew, who publicly announced her death, has reportedly been fired as head of security for the country legend, according to a termination notice obtained by TMZ .
The notice informed Bryan Seaver that he and his security companies had been immediately dismissed from all Dolly properties, TMZ reported.
